title: Compliance export orchestration and tenant-aware reporting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a secure, tenant-aware export pipeline for compliance reports (PDF/CSV/JSON) that respects data residency and retention policies, supports scheduled and on-demand delivery, and produces verifiable evidence bundles with an auditable manifest.

Scope:
- Export formats: CSV for raw logs/rows, PDF for human-readable evidence, JSON for machine consumption.
- Per-tenant residency routing: exports for EU tenants stored in EU regions, US tenants in US regions, with explicit residency metadata in the manifest.
- Retention enforcement: exported artifacts respect the tenant's retention window and trigger TTL deletion from storage and from the console index.
- Scheduled delivery: cron-style schedules (daily/weekly/monthly) and adhoc exports via API/Console.
- Delivery targets: secure S3 buckets (customer-managed or Redwood-managed), email attachments for low-volume reports, and tenant webhooks with retries and signed payloads.
- Evidence bundle: export archive contains report files, manifest.json (signed), generation log, and checksums; manifest includes model of what was filtered/masked, retention epoch, and residency tags.
- Access controls: RBAC so only compliance admins can create schedules or retrieve full evidence; support for time-limited download links and audit log events.
- PII handling: configurable masking rules and sample-redaction for regulated datasets.
- Observability: per-export telemetry (success/failure, latency, bytes, SLO), and dashboard panels in Console for scheduled job health.

Non-goals: building a full document-design engine; complex WYSIWYG templates beyond a templating layer for header/footer and row layout.

Rationale: Several enterprise customers requested a way to automate delivery of retention-compliant artifacts for audits without manual extraction. Current ad-hoc exports are manual and do not include residency metadata or signed manifests, which blocks some regulated customers from adopting Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create scheduled exports with region selection and output format (CSV/PDF/JSON)
Export artifacts include a signed manifest with residency and retention metadata
Exports are stored in the correct region/bucket according to tenant residency setting
Retention TTL is applied to artifacts and metadata indices and deletion is observable in audit logs
Delivery endpoints support Redwood-managed S3 with customer KMS or customer-managed S3, and webhooks with HMAC signatures
Console displays export job health and recent runs; telemetry shows success rate and average generation time
Only users with compliance-admin role can schedule or download full evidence bundles; console applies masking to previewed exports for non-admins
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): build export orchestration service + region-aware storage for hosted customers; internal testing with two pilot accounts
Phase 2: add PDF templating and signed manifest; extend delivery targets to customer S3 with presigned URL flow
Phase 3: RBAC polish, retention automation, and public Console UI for scheduling; open beta with enterprise customers
Phase 4: GA with documentation, SDK helpers, and sample compliance playbook
metrics_and_slos: Export success rate >= 99% for scheduled jobs
Median generation time for up to 100k rows CSV < 60s in Dedicated tier
Manifest verification failures = 0 for valid runs
Scheduled job missed-run rate < 0.1% per week
Time-to-first-delivery (TTFD) for scheduled jobs within SLA window for tenant tier
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-25: Decided to use headless Chromium (puppeteer) for PDF generation to support complex tables and CSS; wkhtmltopdf evaluated but failed on modern CSS layout.
2026-03-02: Chosen approach: reuse exports microservice (ENG-3742) and add region-routing policy layer rather than a separate service to minimize infra overhead.
2026-03-06: Manifest will be JSON-LD style schema v1.0 and signed with Redwood signing key; customers can provide public key for verification if requested.
2026-03-09: For customer-managed S3, use presigned upload endpoints plus server-side verification of bucket region and KMS config during setup flow.
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest schema and signature verification
Integration tests: simulate EU and US tenant exports to verify residency enforcement
Load test: generate 10x expected daily volume to validate batch window and memory usage
Security review: threat model and pen test for delivery endpoints (webhooks/S3)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large PDF generation can OOM on small runners - Mitigation: stream-to-S3 and stepwise rendering, use Dedicated capacity for heavy jobs
Risk: Misconfigured customer S3 bucket causes failed deliveries - Mitigation: pre-validation step and dry-run presigned test object during schedule creation
Risk: GDPR/data residency mismatch - Mitigation: residency routing enforced at orchestration layer with automated audits and daily reconciliation jobs
